input: Research Boeing (boeing.com) for a hedge fund

catalysts.claim: Yahoo Finance estimates Boeing's next earnings report for January 26, 2027; the date is an estimate.
The FAA certified the 737-10 on October 20, 2026; Reuters reports Transport Canada and EASA certification should follow in a couple of months and the first WestJet delivery is slated for early 2027.
Boeing remains on track for first 777X delivery in 2027, with its financial plan assuming certification by mid-2027.

results_vs_guidance.claim: Q3 2026 revenue was $24.188 billion, GAAP diluted loss per share was $0.26, core loss per share was $0.34, operating cash flow was $1.496 billion and free cash flow was $464 million; nine-month free cash flow was negative $359 million.

Yahoo Finance shows Q3 adjusted EPS actual of negative $0.34 versus consensus negative $0.20099, a $0.139 per-share miss; Yahoo's returned historical record did not provide a comparable Q3 revenue consensus.
Management's updated outlook is approximately $2 billion of free cash flow in 2026, $3 billion in 2027, $6 billion in 2028 and $10 billion in 2029; the plan assumes 777X certification by mid-2027.

Management said delayed 737 rate-47 stability would leave 2026 737 deliveries below the 500 target, while 787 deliveries should be 90-100 but closer to the lower end because of the delayed move to rate 10.

event_driven.claim: Boeing was selected by the U.S. Navy to design, build and deliver the F/A-XX next-generation fighter; the order was not yet included in backlog pending completion of source-selection and evaluation review.
Boeing received a seven-year contract award to expand PAC-3 Seeker production and Global Services won an Army award to maintain the AH-64 Apache fleet.

Boeing sold its share of an equity-method investment in Q3 2026 and recorded a $252 million gain; the 10-Q also says Spirit integration was ongoing and Spirit contributed approximately $160 million of Q3 sales.

credit_signals.claim: At September 30, 2026, Boeing had $9.5 billion of cash, $11.2 billion of short-term investments, $45.9 billion of total debt and $10.0 billion of unused revolving credit capacity; it said it remained in compliance with all covenants.
Boeing's credit ratings were investment grade: Fitch BBB- with a positive outlook after a June 2026 revision, S&P BBB- stable and Moody's Baa3 stable.

The August 2026 revolvers mature in August 2027, August 2029 and May 2030; the 364-day facility has a one-year term-out option to August 2028. Boeing also assumed Spirit's $700 million 4.600% notes due 2028 after the $300 million Spirit 2026 notes matured in Q2 2026.

Boeing and Lockheed each agreed to guarantee $750 million of ULA credit facilities maturing August 28, 2029; Boeing expects to provide additional ULA support in Q4 2026 after a Vulcan launch anomaly paused launches.

alternative_signals.claim: Boeing Commercial Airplanes plans to cut about 5% of its workforce through attrition and involuntary layoffs, with notices beginning in December, because slower production ramps left the division overstaffed.
Boeing delivered 161 commercial aircraft in Q3 2026 and 475 year-to-date, including 124 737s and 22 787s in Q3; defense deliveries totaled 33 in Q3.
Commercial Airplanes booked 300 net orders in Q3, including orders from Turkish Airlines, Ethiopian Airlines and Lufthansa; commercial backlog exceeded 6,300 airplanes and was valued at $612 billion.

Boeing reported supplier shortages disrupting factory operations in Q3, adversely affecting KC-46A and 777 Freighter production, with disruption expected to continue into 2027 and create abnormal production costs.

insider_and_ownership.claim: Director Steven M. Mollenkopf bought 2,950 Boeing shares in the open market on October 30 at $173.026 per share; the Form 4 was filed November 3.
Director Mortimer J. Buckley bought 5,820 Boeing shares in the open market on October 30 at $171.55 per share; the Form 4 was filed November 3.
The SEC filings search returned no Boeing SC 13D, SC 13D/A, SC 13G or SC 13G/A filings from November 10, 2025 through November 10, 2026.

risks.claim: The 737 ramp is behind plan: management said rate 47 stability may not be achieved until 2027 and rate 52 is targeted only for the back half of 2027; the 2026 delivery target is consequently expected to be missed.
The 2027-2029 free-cash-flow targets depend on 777X certification by mid-2027; Boeing said 777X will be a significant use of cash in 2027 and turn cash-positive in 2029.

Boeing's 10-Q warns backlog can be reduced by cancellations tied to delivery delays, production disruptions and delayed entry into service of the 777X, 737-7 or 737-10; it also reported $3.164 billion of aircraft order cancellations in the first nine months, primarily 737 and 787.

Boeing said supplier shortages, inflation, labor instability and supplier financial difficulties have reduced productivity and harmed financial position, results and cash flows; it expects the Q3 supplier disruption to continue into 2027.

Boeing's access to capital could be impaired by ratings downgrades, weaker performance, delayed production and delivery ramps or weaker demand; the company also disclosed that U.S. government departments were funded only through December 11, 2026 as of the 10-Q date.

output.research_view: The key debate is execution rather than demand: Boeing has a record $745 billion backlog, 737-10 certification and major defense wins, but its cash-flow plan now depends on stabilizing 737 at 47, reaching 52 in the back half of 2027 and certifying 777X by mid-2027. The most important near-term checks are the January 2027 earnings report, December workforce actions, the pace of 737-10 deliveries and evidence that supplier disruptions and the 787/777 production gaps are clearing.
missing_fields: insider_and_ownership: comprehensive institutional fund position changes from 13F filings
catalysts: exact dates for EASA/Transport Canada 737-10 certification and first WestJet delivery
